title: SSE writer goroutine can use the ResponseWriter after the handler returns
description:
## Symptom

Unrecoverable SIGSEGV in a downstream server (rais, `rais-main`, 2026-08-13 08:13:58):

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
bufio.(*Writer).Flush                          <- nil *bufio.Writer
net/http.(*chunkWriter).flush     server.go:405
net/http.(*response).FlushError   server.go:1729
velox/go.(*gzipResponseWriter).Flush   gzip.go:38
eventsource.WriteEvent                 encoder_write.go:52
velox/go.(*eventSourceTransport).send.func1  transport_sse.go:95
```

## Cause

`send()` runs `eventsource.WriteEvent` on its own goroutine so a stalled client
cannot block the pusher. On `writeTimeout` it sets `writerAbandoned` and
returns — but the goroutine is still inside `Write`/`Flush` holding the
`http.ResponseWriter`.

`conn.Push()` then calls `c.Close()` -> `transport.close()`, which closes
`es.connected`, unblocking `wait()` and returning the HTTP handler. `net/http`
runs `conn.finalFlush()`, which sets `c.bufw = nil`. When the abandoned write
finally unblocks (89s later in the incident) it calls `Flush()` and
dereferences the nil `*bufio.Writer`.

A `ResponseWriter` must never be touched after `ServeHTTP` returns.

## Fix

- `drain()` on the transport: block until no writer goroutine holds the
  ResponseWriter. Called from `conn.Wait()` and the initial-ping failure path,
  so the handler cannot return while a write is in flight.
- best-effort `http.ResponseController.SetWriteDeadline` per send, so the drain
  is bounded by `writeTimeout` instead of by the client's TCP behaviour.
- release the gzip writer in `drain()` rather than `close()`, once it is
  provably unused.
